newsitem.title: UK: IEA says "deeply regrets" German oil sale plan.
newsitem.headline: IEA says "deeply regrets" German oil sale plan.

text.p: The International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Thursday it deeply regretted a German government plan to sell oil from strategic stocks to raise 400 million marks ($230 million) this year.
"We deeply regret this," said a spokesman for the Paris-based agency which was established in the wake of the 1974 oil price shock to protect consuming nations against price rises.
German government sources said on Thursday further oil sales would take place next year but did not say how much revenue it expected to gain or the volume involved.

Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said last month Bonn was considering selling 7.3 million tonnes of oil financed and controlled by the government and held in salt caverns near the northern port of Wilhelmshaven since 1975.

The sale of the federal government's entire crude reserve would still leave Germany with the minimum 90 days of imports required by the IEA, which are held by a Hamburg-based agency on behalf of German oil companies.
IEA director Robert Priddle said in June he regretted a decision by a U.S. House of Representatives committee to sell $209 million worth of oil from the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve in 1998.
